title: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence Against Mohammad Naderi
content:
According to HRANA, the death sentence against Mohammad Naderi has been upheld. Based on information received by HRANA, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence of Mohammad Naderi, who is currently held in Ward 3, Hall 37 of Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj. He had previously been sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court on charges of “espionage.”

An informed source close to Naderi’s family told HRANA: “Using Starlink satellite internet, photographing certain locations, and sending images to media outlets abroad were among the allegations brought against him and served as the basis for his death sentence.”

Naderi was arrested by security forces in Tehran on March 17, 2026, amid war-related security developments, and transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison. He was subsequently transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in October of this year.

title: January 2026 Protests: Omran Amani Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Omran Amani has been sentenced to death. The sentence was issued by Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, and communicated to Amani in prison on Saturday, October 24, 2026. Under the ruling, the 21-year-old was sentenced to death on charges of “moharebeh” (waging war against God).

Omran Amani, a native of Kurdistan Province, had previously moved to Tehran in search of employment. He was arrested by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026 and is currently held in the Greater Tehran Prison.

HRANA is investigating further details regarding the specific allegations underlying the charge against him and the legal proceedings in his case.

title: Tehran Revolutionary Court Sentences Three More Detainees from January Protests to Death
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Amirreza Rezaei, Vahid Ghahremani, and a cleric named Mehdi (surname unknown) were sentenced to death by Branch 23 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Among the charges brought against the three individuals in this case is allegedly carrying out operations on behalf of Israel. The death sentences were communicated to them in prison on Monday, October 26, 2026.

Mehdi, another defendant in the case, is a cleric and a former member of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He has also been sentenced to death by the Special Clerical Court in a separate case on charges of “apostasy.” Consequently, two death sentences have been issued against him in two separate cases.

The three individuals were arrested separately by security forces during the nationwide protests of January 2026.

On Wednesday, October 28, 2026, they were transferred from the Greater Tehran Prison to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj.

title: Nabi Omidi Sentenced to Nine Years in Prison Following Appeals Court Ruling
content:
According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Nabi Omidi has been upheld in full on appeal.

According to information obtained by HRANA, Branch One of the Ilam Province Court of Appeals upheld Mr. Omidi’s nine-year prison sentence on charges including “acting against national security,” “propaganda against the regime,” and “participation in protests.” Under Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, five years of this sentence will be enforceable.

Mr. Omidi had previously been sentenced by judicial authorities to imprisonment, a travel ban prohibiting him from leaving the country, and a ban on entering Malekshahi County. He was also dismissed from Payame Noor University in Ilam in January 2026, amid nationwide protests.

Among the allegations cited against Mr. Omidi was “standing alongside the people of Malekshahi during the January protests.”

In January 2026, amid nationwide protests, Nabi Omidi was arrested by security forces in Ilam and subsequently transferred to the city’s prison.

The report provides no further details about the case, including the judicial authorities responsible for issuing the imprisonment and dismissal orders or the full range of charges brought against him.
snippet: According to HRANA, the sentence issued against Nabi Omidi has been upheld in full on appeal.

title: Amin Ghanbari Sentenced to 20 Years in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, citing Modara, Amin Ghanbari has been sentenced to imprisonment.

According to the report, Branch One of the Semnan Revolutionary Court sentenced Mr. Ghanbari to 20 years in prison on charges of “engaging in media activities against the Islamic Republic,” “assembly and collusion against national security,” “propaganda against the regime,” “supporting the Pahlavi and those killed during the January 2026 protests,” and “insulting the founder of the Islamic Republic.”

Ghanbari was arrested by security forces outside his home in April–May 2026.

The report provides no further information regarding the details of his case, the evidence supporting the charges brought against him, or his current place of detention.

Amin Ghanbari, a resident of Semnan, previously managed the Telegram channel “Payam-Goo-ye Semnan” (Semnan Messenger).

title: Five Prisoners Executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad
content:
According to HRANA, citing Haal Vsh, at least five prisoners were executed in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

Three of the prisoners have been identified as Habibollah Davoodi, 26, a married father of four young children from Zahedan; Alireza Afagh, approximately 26, single, and a resident of Khalqabad village near Mashhad; and Rasoul Irak (Brahui), 67, a father of seven residing in Galikesh County, Golestan Province, and originally from Sistan and Baluchestan Province.

According to the report, Mr. Davoodi was arrested in Mashhad in 2023 and transferred to Vakilabad Prison in the city. He was subsequently sentenced to death by the Mashhad Revolutionary Court on drug-related charges.

On Monday, October 26, Mr. Davoodi was transferred to solitary confinement in preparation for his execution. He was hanged at dawn on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, without prior notification to his family or the opportunity for a final visit.

title: One Prisoner Executed in Sabzevar Prison
content:
According to HRANA, one prisoner was executed in Sabzevar Prison, Razavi Khorasan province, at dawn on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

The identity of the prisoner has been confirmed by HRANA as Reza Talebi. According to information obtained by HRANA, Mr. Talebi had previously been arrested on murder charges and subsequently sentenced to death by a criminal court.

As of the time of this report, the execution has not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

Between October 10, 2025, and October 8, 2026, HRANA documented at least 2,003 executions across Iran, based on 1,857 reports, representing an increase of approximately 29% compared to the previous reporting period. During the same period, HRANA also documented 230 death sentences. For more detailed statistics and analysis of executions in Iran, read HRANA’s latest comprehensive report.
snippet: According to HRANA, one prisoner was executed in Sabzevar Prison, Razavi Khorasan province, at dawn on Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

title: Nemat Afshar Arrested in Qazvin
content:
Based on information received by HRANA, Nemat Afshar was arrested on Monday, October 26, 2026, at his residence in Qazvin by local IRGC Intelligence agents.

A source close to his family confirmed the news to HRANA, stating: “About a month ago, the relevant authorities contacted Mr. Afshar’s bail guarantor regarding his previous conviction and informed them that he was required to report to prison to serve his sentence. However, no precise information has yet been obtained regarding the reason for Nemat Afshar’s arrest or his whereabouts. This uncertainty has raised concerns among his family and relatives.”

In April 2025, the Court of Appeals upheld Mr. Afshar’s sentence of three years and six months in prison, along with a two-year travel ban and a two-year prohibition on online activities.

In November 2024, Nemat Afshar, along with three other individuals, Azam Ahooghalandar, Hossein Jafari, and Mehdi Touhidi, was sentenced by Branch 3 of the Karaj Revolutionary Court in a joint case. The four defendants received a combined total of 14 years and 10 months in prison, along with additional penalties.

Nemat Afshar is unmarried and resides in Qazvin.
snippet: Based on information received by HRANA, Nemat Afshar was arrested on Monday, October 26, 2026, at his residence in Qazvin by local IRGC Intelligence agents.

title: Two Prisoners Executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj
content:
According to HRANA, two prisoners were executed in Ghezel Hesar Prison.

HRANA has confirmed the identities of the prisoners as Amrollah Seiri, a resident of Varamin, and Shokri (first name unknown), a resident of Markazi Province. Both prisoners were hanged at dawn today, Wednesday, October 28, 2026.

According to information obtained by HRANA, the two prisoners had previously been arrested on murder charges in separate cases and were subsequently sentenced to death by criminal courts.

As of the time of this report, the executions have not been officially announced by prison authorities or other relevant institutions.

title: Artin Ghazanfari, Baha’i Citizen, Sentenced to 26 Years in Prison
content:
Under a verdict issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, and communicated to him on Monday, Artin Ghazanfari was sentenced to a total of 26 years in prison.

An informed source close to Ghazanfari’s family told HRANA: “Mr. Ghazanfari was sentenced to 20 years in prison on the charge of ‘media-related activities,’ five years for ‘assembly and collusion against national security,’ and one year for ‘propaganda against the regime.’ Although the punishment for the first charge was stated to be 10 years in prison, the judge imposed a 20-year sentence by invoking the Law on Intensifying Punishment for Espionage.”

According to information obtained by HRANA, Ghazanfari’s physical condition has been reported as poor due to several medical conditions, including heart failure, asthma, and high blood pressure. Despite prison medical staff emphasizing the necessity of transferring him to medical facilities outside the prison, he continues to be denied access to specialized medical treatment outside the prison due to opposition from the judge overseeing his case.
